8683.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM4761 : Medical Embedded Systems Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. Introduction to Arduino and ATmega328P Microcontroller Basics: Familiarize with the Arduino environment and ATmega328P microcontroller set up a simple LED control program to understand basic GPIO.
2. Interrupt Handling on ATmega328P: Implement foreground and background processing with basic interrupts configure external and timer interrupts to control LEDs or buzzer.
3. Serial Communication with ATmega328P: Explore USART communication by establishing serial data transfer between the Arduino and a computer, displaying sensor data on the serial monitor.
4. Digital Communication Protocols: I2C and SPI: Interface an I2C-based sensor (e.g., temperature sensor) and an SPI-based peripheral (e.g., SD card module) with ATmega328P to read data from each.
5. Working with GPIO: Debouncing and Digital Signal Control- Implement a debounced push-button using GPIO and examine digital signal control techniques by configuring GPIO pins in push-pull and open-drain modes.
6. Timer Configuration and PWM Generation: Configure the ATmega328P’s timers to generate PWM signals control the brightness of an LED or the speed of a motor using PWM.
7. Power Management and Sleep Modes: Implement various sleep modes in ATmega328P to reduce power consumption measure and compare power usage in different modes.
8. Reset Logic and Watchdog Timer: Explore ATmega328P’s reset mechanisms by implementing and testing Power-On-Reset, External Reset, and Watchdog Timer Reset.
9. Memory Management and EEPROM Usage: Understand memory subsystems in ATmega328P by reading and writing data to EEPROM develop a simple data logger that stores data in EEPROM.
10. Op-Amp Fundamentals and Biosignal Front-End Circuit Design: Design and test a basic op-amp-based biosignal amplifier circuit, such as an instrumentation amplifier for recording biosignals (e.g., ECG).
11. Analog-to-Digital Conversion and Signal Sampling: Configure the ATmega328P’s ADC to sample an analog signal, understand quantization noise, and observe ADC performance on biosignal data.
12. Edge AI Deployment on Arduino Nano BLE Sense: Deploy a small-scale AI model on the Nano BLE Sense to classify biosignals or sensor data (e.g., motion classification using accelerometer data). This experiment will include model training on a PC, quantization for embedded deployment, and inference on the Nano BLE Sense, highlighting resource constraints and model optimization for embedded AI applications.

Course Objective

1 .

Develop Proficiency in Embedded System Programming and Peripheral Interfacing.
2 .

Explore Power Management, Memory Handling, and Analog Circuit Design for Biosignal Applications.
3 .

Apply Embedded AI Techniques and Real-Time Processing for Smart Medical Applications.

Course Outcome

1 .

After the completion of this course, the student will be able to:
1. Design and implement embedded systems using microcontrollers for various applications.
2. Acquire, process, and analyze biosignals for healthcare and biomedical applications.
3. Optimize power consumption in embedded systems for energy-efficient solutions.
4. Deploy AI models on edge devices for real-time decision-making in healthcare and other domains.
5. Utilize non-volatile memory for data storage and retrieval in embedded systems.

6379.t: CE6033: Numerical Methods in Civil Engineering
6379.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6033 : Numerical Methods in Civil Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to Numerical Methods(2 hours)
Why study numerical methods Sources of error in numerical solutions: truncation error round off error Order of accuracy - Taylor series expansion

Module 2 :

Direct Solution of Linear systems (4 hours)
Gauss elimination Gauss Jordan elimination Pivoting, inaccuracies due to pivoting Factorization Cholesky decomposition Diagonal dominance condition number, ill conditioned matrices, singularity and singular value decomposition Banded matrices, storage schemes for banded matrices, skyline solver

Module 3 :

Iterative solution of Linear systems (3 hours)
Jacobi iteration Gauss Seidel iteration Convergence criteria

Module 4 :

Direct Solution of Non Linear systems (4 hours)
Newton Raphson iterations to find roots of a 1D nonlinear equation Generalization to multiple dimensions Newton Iterations Quasi Newton iterations Local and global minimum rates of convergence convergence criteria.

Module 5 :

Iterative Solution of Non Linear systems (3 hours)
Conjugate gradient Preconditioning.

Module 6 :

Partial Differential Equations (4 hours)
Introduction to partial differential equations Definitions & classifications of first and second order equations Examples of analytical solutions Method of characteristics.

Module 7 :

Numerical Differentiation (4 hours)
Difference operators (forward, backward and central difference) Stability and accuracy of solutions Application of finite difference operators to solve initial and boundary value problems.
Module 8 :

Introduction to the Finite Element Method as a method to solve partial differential equations (6 hours)
Strong form of the differential equation Weak form Galerkin method: the finite element approximation Interpolation functions: smoothness, continuity completeness, Lagrange polynomials Numerical quadrature: Trapezoidal rule, Simpsons rule, Gauss quadrature

Module 9 :

Numerical integration of time dependent partial differential equations (4 hours)
Parabolic equations: algorithms - stability consistency and convergence, Lax equivalence theorem Hyperbolic equations: algorithms - Newmark's method,stability and accuracy, convergence, multi-step methods

Module 10 :

Numerical solutions of integral equations (6 hours)
Types of integral equations, Fredholm integral equations of the first and second kind, Fredholm's Alternative theorem Collocation and Galerkin methods for solving integral equations

Course Objective

1 .

Understanding core concepts of error estimate and accuracy of numerical solutions. It then introduces the student to methods of solution of linear and non-linear equations.Both direct and iterative solution methods are discussed.
2 .

Introduction to the numerical solution of partial differential equations, after a brief review of canonical partial differential equations and well known analytical techniques for their solution, stressing when and why numerical solutions are necessary Introduction to Finite difference operators to solve typical initial and boundary value problems.
3 .

Introduction to the finite element method as a generic method for the numerical solution of partial differential equations. The concepts of weak form, finite element discretization, polynomial interpolation using Lagrange polynomials and numerical quadrature are introduced.
4 .

Numerical integration in the time domain emphasizing the key requirements of stability and accuracy of time integration algorithms. Introduction to integral equations and numerical techniques for their solution.

Course Outcome

1 .

Understand and apply various numerical methods for solving mathematical problems.

2 .

Analyze the accuracy, efficiency, and stability of numerical algorithms.
3 .

Implement numerical methods using programming languages and software tools.

4 .

Students will learn how to apply, analyze, and implement various iterative methods.

5 .

Students will be equipped to handle a wide variety of real-world computational problems involving linear systems of equations

Essential Reading

Timothy Sauer, Numerical Analysis, Pearson Education Inc, Boston, MA

2 .

D. Dahlquist, and A. Bork, Numerical Methods, Prentice-Hall, Englewood Cliffs, NJ

2 .

Module 1 :

Module1: Introduction:
Introduction to the industrial instrumentation, Need for industrial instrumentation, Industrial process variables, Types of instruments, Functional elements of an instrument, Static & dynamic characteristics of an instrument.
4 Hours
Module 2: Pressure measurement:
Introduction to pressure measurement,
Measurement of mid-range pressures – U-tube manometer, Dead-weight gauge, Diaphragm, Bellows, Bourdon tube,
Low- pressure measurement - McLeod gauge, Thermal conductivity gauge, Ionization gauge,
High pressure measurement – Bridgman gauge.

Thermal expansion methods – Liquid-in-glass thermometer, Bimetallic thermometer, Pressure thermometer,
Thermoelectric sensors – Thermocouple,
Varying-resistance devices – Resistance thermometers, Thermistors,
Radiation methods – Radiation fundamentals, Radiation thermometers – Unchopped broad-band radiation thermometer, Chopped broad-band radiation thermometer, Narrow-band radiation thermometer, Optical pyrometer, Two-color radiation thermometer, Blackbody-tipped fiber optic radiation thermometer.
7 Hours

Introduction to flow measurement, Laminar and turbulent flow, Total energy and conservation of energy, Types of flow meters, Close channel and open channel flow meters. Methods of flow measurement.
Differential pressure flow meters – Orifice, Nozzle, Venturi tube, Dall flow tube, Pitot tube,
Variable-area flow meter, Turbine flow meter, Vortex shedding flow meter, Positive displacement flow meter,
Noninvasive methods – Electromagnetic flow meter, Ultrasonic flow meter, Laser-Doppler flow meter.
7 Hours
Module 5: Level measurement:
Introduction to level measurement,
Different level instruments: Dip Sticks, Float systems, Pressure measuring devices, Ultrasonic level gauge, Capacitive devices, Radiation methods, Thermal effect types, Electrical methods.
4 Hours

Introduction to fiber optic sensors, principle of optical fiber, Fiber optic sensors: Extrinsic sensor, Intrinsic sensor, Intensity modulated sensor, Phase modulated sensor, Frequency modulated sensor, Wavelength modulated sensor, Polarization modulated sensor, Scattering loss modulated sensor.
5 Hours

Humidity, Chemical composition, PH measurement, some recent advancement.
3 Hours

To make students familiar with the measurement of pressure, temperature, flow, level, humidity, and chemical compositions.

Experiment 1: Create the shape shown using Ansys workbench and extrude it to form a solid. Choose your own dimensions. Use the Sketching Trim option to help in the sketch development. Save it, and we’ll use it in a simulation problem later in the text. 2 Hours

Subject {L-T-P / C} : LS5410 : Molecular Genetics { 3-0-0 / 3}

Syllabus

Module 2 :

Linkage and gene mapping; Tetrad analysis.; Molecular markers and somatic cell hybrids; Extranuclear inheritance and organellar genetics; Maternal inheritance.

Mutation: Types, causes, and detection; Genetic implications of mutations; Ploidy: Aneuploidy and Euploidy (Autopolyploidy and Allopolyploidy); Chromosomal segregation in ploidy; Chromosomal rearrangements: Inversions, translocations, deletions, and duplications.

Master Mendelian inheritance, pedigree analysis, and complex deviations like genomic imprinting and polygenic traits.
2 .

Utilize linkage, molecular markers, and tetrad analysis to construct accurate genetic and physical maps.
3 .

Categorize mutation types and chromosomal rearrangements to assess their structural and functional genetic impacts.
4 .

Apply Hardy-Weinberg principles to evaluate population dynamics, speciation mechanisms, and molecular evolutionary trends.

Course Outcome

1 .

Evaluate Mendelian laws, pedigree patterns, and complex deviations like genomic imprinting and polygenic inheritance.
2 .

Apply gene mapping techniques, molecular markers, and tetrad analysis to determine genetic positioning.
3 .

Analyze molecular mutations, chromosomal rearrangements, and the biological consequences of altered ploidy levels.
4 .

Synthesize population genetic data using Hardy-Weinberg principles to explain speciation and molecular evolution.
